terra.problem: Saying the invitation leads somewhere Amaziah did not plan adds a detail about his plans that the text does not give.
“Wrong direction” says “wrong” about the baker’s answer.
The closing line about not wanting to be the plant is a flat, generic reaction to a moment that can hold a real laugh.
The story does not say the cedar stays standing or never moves. It only says a wild beast tramples the thistle.
“What they did to his heart” makes Amaziah’s words the cause of his pride. Jehoash connects the pride to his defeat of Edom, not to his words.
Jehoash gives this warning in a reply to Amaziah’s message. The text does not say he speaks it straight to Amaziah’s face.
The closing thought about staying home is generic and misses a clear opportunity for Papa Dorin’s humor.
“The whole kingdom goes down” overstates Jehoash’s warning and presents its conditional outcome as a fact.
Edom being Judah’s neighbor is a Bible-related fact from outside this passage, but no supporting reference is given.
The text does not say Amaziah stayed in place or that his face-to-face meeting with Jehoash was long.
The passage does not say there were no guards on the wall or that Jehoash did not station guards there.
“The wall doesn’t survive” suggests the whole wall was destroyed, although the next sentence correctly says only a section came down.
The passage does not say the house of God and the palace treasuries were both emptied.
Calling Samaria Israel’s capital adds a Bible-related fact from outside the passage without a supporting reference.
“The conspiracy in Jerusalem sends him running” states why Amaziah fled, but the text does not explicitly give his reason.
